items.title: La La Land
items.review: “People love what other people are passionate about” - Mia Seeing this in theaters just completed me!! Watching this movie now at this age makes me relate to Seb & Mia and the emotions in the feeling, desire, and aspiration that most have in their 20s, and what’s worse is the million rejections and emotions that throttle animating aspects of life. The dreams The colors just wow. I don’t think seeing this at home or anywhere else besides the theatres does it justice. Also, the nostalgic feeling omg the Prius, the 2016 elements, the palm trees, and the atmosphere - it’s like a small snapshot of my childhood perception of LA. It’s heartbreaking to say the least. it doesn’t exist anymore with Palisades Fire and the pandemic and many socioeconomic things. it kinda brings you back to that city of stars portrayed is a dreamy place that no longer exists just like in the movies. 🙁💔 I don’t wanna be like Seb and cling to that restorative nostalgia, but I would forever cherish the reflective nostalgia this movie brings me every time I see it in the context of my life. 🤍 I think we’re all somewhat Seb and Mia in our little lives. We hang posters, read books, and watch films that remind us of nostalgia. (Unironically, me watching the 10th anniversary of a movie that I somewhat grew old with.) We all cling to it like Mia’s obsession with old Hollywood and Seb’s dream to restore jazz. Each rebellious to the times and dreamer of their own future. Here’s to the ones who dream, Foolish as they may seem. Here’s to the hearts that ache. Here’s to the mess we make. - Mia

I just pretend to be."

items.title: A Tribe Called Love
items.review: Warra a watch. I think this is one of the most deeply personal experiences I felt with a movie in a longtime. The people I talked to after the film itself, the messaging. The film really did highlights the problems we see plaguing our community, in such a beautiful and comedic way. I remember speaking to a fellow peer of mine that watched the movie as well, and then I asked them, "Hey, what do you think about the movie?" We're casually talking about some of the plot points that were devastating and are actually impacting our lives as well, like gun violence in that aspect. It just shows how prevalent the issue is really. One personal message the director mentioned during Q&A that really stuck with me was the stubborn nature of Somali men and how, in our ways, we tend to harm ourselves or kill ourselves in the process rather than coming together. I'm just super excited for Somali cinema in general. I think seeing this film and the production level, the quality, the acting, I'm just excited for what's coming next, the next wave. I'm ngl, this might be up there for sure, especially for Somali cinema. This is the bar to beat. The animation was superb. Just wowed me; seemed like a personal love letter to Somalia and Toronto. The timeline on this was just nuts: 23 days, 8 hours a day of shooting. Just hearing this is just top-notch stuff, man. I can't wait to see all the other stuff from Mawimbi and Mohammed himself, Phenomenal Film. If you’re an Aspiring SOMALI CINEPHILE PICKUP THE CAMERA and shoot something, LIKE MOHAMED said. 🩵🇸🇴
